summary: Swing for the whole song: up to eight steps, each tick's length scaled by its step's factor in turn.
use_for: Swing for the whole song: up to eight steps that stretch or squeeze each tick.
quirks: It changes the song's timing, not its sound; it sets the master's groove pattern (ReBuzz/Core/ReBuzzCore.cs SetGroovePattern) when a parameter changes.
The pattern is normalised so its average is 1: only the ratios between steps matter, and with every step at 1.0x (all raw 0) nothing swings.
Steps above Steps in groove are ignored; 0 steps is off.
Step length is 1.0 + raw x 2 / 127, so 3.0x at raw 127; the machine's own description gives the formula but no unit.
evidence: Machines/ReBuzzGroove/ReBuzzGroove.cs — the machine's source: its declarations, Work and menu
ReBuzz/Core/ReBuzzCore.cs — SetGroovePattern: zero lengths become 1 and the pattern is scaled to an average of 1

parameters.name: NumSteps
parameters.description: Number of steps in Groove. 0 = off. 0 is off
parameters.how: Sets how many of the eight steps are used, 0 to 8; 0 (the default) turns the groove off.
parameters.sound: More steps make a longer swing pattern that repeats over the song; with 0 the timing is straight.

parameters.name: Step1
parameters.description: Tick speed multiplyer = 1.0f + value * 2.0f / 127.0f. This step's tick lasts this many ticks
parameters.how: Sets how long step 1 lasts relative to the others, 1.0x (raw 0, the default) to 3.0x (raw 127); only the ratios between steps matter, because the pattern is scaled to keep the average at 1.
parameters.sound: A step above its neighbours is stretched and one below is squeezed, so notes landing on step 1 come late or early against the grid; all steps equal means no swing.
